hints: Notice the options differ by whether change of momentum or mass x change in speed is divided by or multiplied by time taken.
Recall that momentum $p = mv$ is a vector, while speed is a scalar, so a definition of vector force must involve momentum.
Check units: force in $\text{N}$ equals $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$, which is momentum $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$ divided by time $\text{s}$.
walkthrough: Identify what is offered: option B uses mass x change in speed over time, while options C and D use change of momentum with time.
State the governing definition from Newton's second law: resultant force equals rate of change of momentum, $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$.
Explain why momentum is needed: momentum is $p = mv$ as a vector, so $\Delta p$ correctly includes direction, whereas change in speed alone does not.
Check division versus multiplication: dividing $\Delta p$ in $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$ by time in $\text{s}$ gives $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$, which is $\text{N}$, while multiplying gives $\text{N s}^2$.
Conclude that only change of momentum divided by time taken matches the definition. This is option D.

options.A: Multiplying by time taken gives units of $\text{kg m}$, not newtons, so this cannot be force.
options.B: This gives $m \Delta v / \Delta t$ which equals $ma$ for constant mass, but it uses scalar speed and is not the general definition using momentum.
options.C: Multiplying change of momentum by time taken gives $\Delta p \times \Delta t$, which has units $\text{N s}^2$ and is not force.
options.D: Newton's second law defines force as rate of change of momentum, $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$.
